result.title: Nash-MOPD: Optimizing Task Trade-offs in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) aggregates the capabilities of multiple domain-expert teachers into a single student model. However, all domains in MOPD share the student's finite budget of optimization steps and rollouts. Fixed uses constant domain sampling ratios based on corpus sizes; by contrast, D$^3$-MOPD adjusts the ratios using the teacher-student reverse-KL divergence and its recent decrease. However, favoring large recent decreases can direct more training toward domains that already improve quickly, while domains that improve more slowly may receive too few examples. To address inflexible allocation and the risk of giving insufficient training to domains that improve more slowly, we propose Nash-MOPD, an adaptive domain scheduler based on a local minimax game using existing reverse-KL statistics. The equilibrium maximizes the smallest predicted proportional reduction under the local model and gives more prompts to domains that need more examples for comparable improvement. Consequently, Nash-MOPD responds to changing learning progress and supports domains that improve more slowly without extra teacher queries or rollouts. At step 100, Nash-MOPD exceeds both baselines' final mathematics and code checkpoint scores on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and reaches Fixed's on Qwen3-8B-Base. Furthermore, it leads eight of nine reported metrics and is best or tied best on all six mathematics and code accuracy metrics, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Nash-MOPD：在多教师在线蒸馏（MOPD）中，用局部极小极大博弈与已有的 reverse-KL 统计自适应调整各领域的采样比例，使进步较慢的领域获得更多提示，从而在不增加教师查询和 rollout 的前提下改善数学与代码等领域的蒸馏效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按领域公平分配优化步数的极小极大调度思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中多类监督或多阶段行为（如 THINK/LOOK/STOP）的预算分配与贡献分配问题；但原文只研究纯文本多教师蒸馏，与视觉 latent 状态生成无直接关联。
